publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on EMC in Electric Traction and Signalling
abstract: This presentation is primarily concerned with the measurement of electric and magnetic fields radiated from arcs produced on London Underground trains when the pick-up shoe separates from the conductor rail at gaps between sections of the conductor rail. The characteristics of arcs within the London Underground environment have been studied with the aim of proposing methods for detection and subsequent suppression. This work was part of that programme.

articleTitle: Computation of electromagnetic fields in the vicinity of a railway catenary
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on EMC in Electric Traction and Signalling
abstract: An understanding of the influence of railway power systems on the local electromagnetic environment is of importance to ensure that such installations will satisfy the protection requirements of the EMC regulations. Although these characteristics must ultimately be demonstrated experimentally, the ability to make predictions in advance could help to establish emissions specifications for on-board systems. Here, the author describes how, in order to investigate the potential for such analysis, measurements are being undertaken by GEC ALSTHOM Metro Cammell, in collaboration with GEC ALSTHOM Traction. These results are compared with theoretical values computed using SLIM, an electromagnetic field modelling package developed by GEC ALSTHOM Engineering Research Centre.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on EMC in Electric Traction and Signalling
abstract: This paper looks at a few EMC type testing topics related to compliance with the new Railway Standard ENV50121. The author has been working on EMC compliance programs for existing equipment for 9 months. The installation of an EMC test facility for full compliance testing has been part of this task. It is hoped that the ideas are useful to others embarking on the same road. The author discusses type test documentation, external test house testing, EMC test design, fast transient surge, surge susceptibility, conducted RF susceptibility, and radiated RF susceptibility.

articleTitle: The standards are coming hurrah! hurrah? [railway EMC]
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on EMC in Electric Traction and Signalling
abstract: The author describes how European standards-making body CENELEC has a Railway Committee TC9X and this decided that EMC product standards were required for railways. A series of pre-standards in the ENV 50121 series will be in effect from 15 January 1996, covering EMC aspects of emission and immunity at power and radio frequencies. The limits proposed take account of the actual measured values from existing designs of equipment.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on EMC in Electric Traction and Signalling
abstract: The management of electromagnetic compatibility has become a crucial element in the design of each and every electrical and electronic system. All of the sub-systems installed to provide the facilities expected of a modern railway system must operate in harmony, without any form of undesirable interaction. Amongst numerous compatibility issues within the modern railway, ensuring the compatibility of the modern electric vehicle with existing signalling systems has proved difficult. Unless certain precautions are taken, the electronic switching techniques used in the conversion and control of AC traction on modern electric vehicles can cause interference, affecting the safe operation of some types of train detection devices used within the signalling system. ABB Signal Limited has developed two types of fail-safe interference monitor for the real time measurement of interference signals within the traction return current to remove interference and maintain the safety of the signalling system.

articleTitle: Noise cancellation in train distribution systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on EMC in Electric Traction and Signalling
abstract: Harmonics problems in railway power distribution systems are discussed by the author. Three techniques have been described for cancelling unwanted harmonics on high current, high voltage railway power systems and areas for further investigation have been outlined.
